history.dynasty: None (BAPS - Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha)
history.summary: The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir at Wathoda on Swaminarayan Marg, Middle Ring Road, Nagpur, is a modern shikharbaddh mandir of the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha. Pramukh Swami Maharaj sowed the seeds of satsang in the Vidarbha region on a 1976 visit; he performed the murti-pratishtha of a hari mandir at Vardhmannagar in 1993 and inaugurated The Swaminarayan School in 1997. The groundbreaking for the shikharbaddh mandir at Wathoda was performed in 2004, and the murti-pratishtha of the completed mandir was performed in 2013 - inaugurated on 7 October 2013 as reportedly the 750th Swaminarayan temple in India, with 80% of construction cost from local devotees' donations. The complex spans over 11 acres with intricately carved sandstone columns, pinnacles and domes in traditional haveli-influenced architecture, plus a dining area and assembly hall. A strict modest dress code is enforced; photography is restricted beyond a point on the approach path.

name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
town_description: Nagpur is the winter capital and second capital of Maharashtra, the largest city of the Vidarbha region and a major commercial and transport hub, famous for its oranges (the 'Orange City'). It is a premier rail junction linking all four metropolitan cities of India and is served by the Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport. Wathoda, in the eastern part of the city on the Middle Ring Road, is home to the modern BAPS mandir complex.

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur; 12 km from the mandir (per official BAPS visitor info).
travel.railway: Nagpur Railway Station (Nagpur Junction); 8 km from the mandir (per official BAPS visitor info).
travel.road: Swaminarayan Marg, Middle Ring Road, Wathoda, Nagpur 440030; 7 km from the city bus station (per BAPS). Taxis, app cabs and auto-rickshaws available; private parking at the complex.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Diwali and Annakut are the grandest celebrations; the Saturday/Sunday 7:30 PM light and sound show is a highlight.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Mandir open 8:00 AM-12:00 noon and 4:00 PM-8:30 PM daily (official BAPS visitor info). Murti darshan: 7:30-10:30 AM, 11:15 AM-12:00 noon, 4:00-6:30 PM, 7:00-8:30 PM; closed 10:30-11:15 AM and 6:30-7:00 PM for Thal. Modest dress (cover shoulders and knees) mandatory; remove footwear at entry.
